title: Statistical Analysis of the Phaistos Disc: A Computational Methodology for Phonetic Key Evaluation
description:
A rigorous computational and statistical framework for evaluating competing phonetic key hypotheses for the Phaistos Disc (~1700 BCE). The study applies Bonferroni-corrected Monte Carlo simulation across 9 candidate keys scored against three reference corpora: Luwian Hieroglyphic vocabulary, Linear A frequency tables, and the AED-TEI Egyptian corpus (675,773 tokens from 13,950 texts). Two strictly separated transcription systems are used: Evans/Godart canonical (45 signs, 241 tokens, 61 word-groups) for key-independent structural analysis, and Achterberg phonetic for G_LUWIAN phonetic scoring.

Four key-independent findings are established on Evans/Godart canonical data: (1) PLUMED HEAD→SHIELD bigram Z=+12.05 excess adjacency (obs/exp=9.7×, p<0.0001, MC n=20,000, null: frequencies preserved, adjacency randomised); (2) PLUMED HEAD 100% word-initial across all 19 occurrences (Z=+7.51, p<0.0001); (3) formulaic refrain structure — 7 repeated word-group sequences (refrain density 24.6%, Z=+45.60, p<0.0001), consistent with ritual text classification (corpus domain control: theological Z=+27 vs administrative Z=−0.4); (4) sign #46 100% word-final in 18/18 occurrences (Z=+7.64, p=2×10⁻¹⁴). All four are robust across all parameter thresholds tested. A fifth structural comparison (§5.7) is reported as a directional indicator only, limited by small reference corpora (47–48 word-forms).

The Luwian Hieroglyphic key (G_LUWIAN, Achterberg 2004 transcription) achieves the highest Bonferroni-significant score among all 9 keys (p<0.0001). A blind corpus key test (200,000 trials) draws random syllable assignments from the TLHdig top-50 attested syllable pool; zero trials reach the G_LUWIAN score (Z=+8.53, p<0.000005). An ablation study removing all wa-tar compounds reduces Z by only 10% (Z=+8.53→+7.54). The Achterberg transcription is not a neutral baseline (it encodes Luwian assumptions); the four key-independent pillars use Evans/Godart and are unaffected by this concern.

A Multi-Language Arena (§6.23) tests 35 language hypotheses; all pass significance — a property of the disc's short words and limited sign inventory, not a language identification claim. Relative ranking is informative; the highest-scoring hybrid is Anatolio-Babylonian (Z=+27.04), compatible with a Kizzuwatna scribal contact zone.

Three cross-validation studies extend the framework: a head-to-head Arena comparison of G_LUWIAN vs Achterberg 2021 (both Bonferroni-significant, statistically indistinguishable, discriminated by semantic coherence); a mirror-symmetry test placing the disc below the administrative-script threshold (28.9% vs Linear A 47.7%); and a Soldani 2013 paleographic cross-validation independently confirming six key-independent claims from a 268-page PhD thesis using no computational tools. Three oath-deity convergences (Tiwat, Išara/JA-SA-SA-RA, Talos) are documented in the Minoan-Anatolian contact zone at ~1800–1700 BCE.

A seasonal covenant calendar synthesis (§7.21) integrates statistical structure, Hittite ritual calendars (CTH 325 twice-yearly Vanishing God), and Bronze Age climate history into a use-hypothesis: the disc as a seasonal maritime covenant instrument read at the autumn and spring equinoxes, with za-wa-tar ('this water') sworn upon a physical water source in the post-4.2-kyr-drought existential context. This section is labeled as a working hypothesis.

All four competing theories with significant scholarly presence are evaluated: Fuls 2019 (Luwian epigraphic), Akulov 2024 (Hattic), Revesz 2020 (Proto-Finno-Ugric), and Owens & Coleman (Linear B, most widely cited in popular media — B_FREQ proxy scores Z=+3.61, below G_LUWIAN). None has been submitted to the Decipherment Arena framework. Eighteen limitations are enumerated, including key design circularity, Achterberg transcription bias, N=1 constraint (shared by all disc research), post-hoc grammatical prediction revision (HARKing acknowledged), and structural fingerprint corpus size. Token-level scores are ~94% frequency-driven; all primary claims rest on key-independent evidence. All code, data, and null results are released open-source for independent replication.
notes: v18.0 adds: §7.11 Decipherment Arena — an open benchmark framework for evaluating any proposed phonetic key against the same Bonferroni-corrected Monte Carlo scoring system used throughout this paper. Any researcher can submit a sign-to-syllable mapping as a Python dictionary; the pipeline scores it against Luwian, Linear A, and Egyptian corpora under identical conditions. This is the primary structural contribution of the paper: not the G_LUWIAN result specifically, but a replicable, language-agnostic evaluation standard applicable to any undeciphered script with a reference corpus. Abstract updated to reflect this framing. v17.0 adds: §7.10.9 updated with Ben-Tor 2007 cross-verification — BEE sign now confirmed in two independent design contexts at Tell el-Dab'a (isolated Gardiner L2 via Ilin-Tomich 2023 + nsw-bít title design class 3B2 via Ben-Tor 2007 nos. 803, 901, stratum D/2); RAM/caprid (9B) count corrected to 4 confirmed examples (Mlinar nos. 1059, 1062, 1064, 1072), tied with crocodile class (9D) — lion class (9E) confirmed absent; new Human Figure row (Design class 10A, 3 examples in early TelD local workshop per Ben-Tor §IIA 10a) added as 5th iconographic alignment; confirmed sign count updated to 4–5 of 45. v16.0 adds: §6.18 Sign #29 (na) connective biclitic reanalysis — original genitive prediction refuted (Z=−4.11); revised connective biclitic prediction confirmed (Z=+3.26); §6.19 Sign #7 (ti) polyvalent copula — unconditional neutral, but ha→ti conditional FINAL confirmed (Z=+3.17, 3/3=100%); B21=B26 clitic chain formula confirmed; §6.20 Non-core signs comprehensive audit (#12=zi indeterminate, #6=an marginal+, #1=i prediction revised to verbal suffix); inversion pattern: WEAK-acrophony signs (#29,#7) rescued by revised structural predictions, CONFIRMED-acrophony signs (#6,#1) marginal; §6.21 Side A complete readability (93.5% of Side A fully readable under 11-sign G_LUWIAN key vs 10% for Side B) — compositional asymmetry quantified; reversed refrain A22 = ha-za-wa-tar identified. Revised Grammatical Position Test: 1/4 → 3/4 confirmed with linguistically-motivated expanded predictions (Wackernagel clitic chains, biclitic particles); §6.22 Side B Egyptian-acrophonic layer test — HIGH-confidence signs Z=+4.98 (p=0.00002) vs Egyptian theological vocabulary; §7.10 Bilateral Maritime Covenant — complete use theory: disc as bilingual trade-safety litany sealing Minoan/Luwian/Egyptian commercial agreements; three of six predictions already confirmed by independent tests; stamp-manufacturing evidence for multi-copy distribution. This work is presented as a methodology paper and a working hypothesis, not a definitive decipherment. All null results are reported transparently. Independent replication by a Luwianologist specialist is required for confirmation.
